text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein undergoes routine health checks in Mayo clinic in USA.
- Israel stops Gazans from crossing King Hussein Bridge between West Bank and Jordan after Tel Aviv explosion, sources say.
- Water minister says government will take all steps to ensure Jordan River water does not get polluted.
- Deterioration in doctors' pay conditions as result of fall in value of incentives.
- Improvement in Iraqi-Jordanian ties. UN approves contracts for Jordanian exports to Iraq -- 10 companies get export approval.
- Crown Prince Hassan calls for dialogue instead of violence in the Middle East peace process.
- Prime Minister Abdul Salam-al-Majali affirms Jordan's keenness to strengthen ties with Iraq.
- Two ministerial committees set up for services and development.
- Planning Ministry official says Jordan nearly reached stage of doing without World Bank support for its economic reform programme.
- Prime Minister hopes World Bank will offer assistance to Jordan to launch small projects and help alleviate poverty.
- Crown Prince Hassan and Prime Minister indicate government focus is on internal issues as well as efforts to end crisis in peace process.
- No strain in Jordanian-Iraqi ties, Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz says after talks with Majali.
